messages:
alex_g: heads-up — canary for qwen2.5 long-context (32k) is showing a ~2.3x p99 latency regression after yesterday's autokernel heuristic change. perf-bot: regression alert fired @ 03:12 UTC.
jin_zhang: saw that alert, grabbing profiler traces now. can you paste the kernel_selector logs?
alex_g: here are the interesting lines from the selector:
```
kernel_selector: model_meta.n_heads=32 model_meta.kv_head_dim=64
inferred_from_weights: heads=64 kv=32
selected_kernel=optimized_attention_v4(heads=64,kv=32)
-> runtime fallback to generic_attention due to head/kv mismatch
```
katie_s: whoa — inferred dims disagree with model metadata. that explains the fallback churn. why is inference reading the wrong dims?
noah: i ran the local repro: `./bin/profiler --model qwen2.5 --seq 32768 --batch 1 --trace kernels` and captured QKV shapes. snippet: `qkv_weight.shape=(3,64,12288) expected_heads=32 expected_kv=64`. looks like our weight unpacking treats second dim as num_heads for some exported checkpoints.
samir: bisect points to 4f2d9c2 — that commit changed autokernel to infer heads from param shapes when model.json is missing or incomplete. for some qwen2.5 checkpoints, the ordering is (n_kv_heads, n_heads, head_dim) instead of (n_heads, n_kv_heads, head_dim).
alex_g: repro curl (canary):
```
curl -s -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"qwen2.5","input":"你好，今天的天气如何？" ,"max_new_tokens":512,"context_length":32768}'
```
This triggers the kernel fallback path ~every request.
katie_s: also noticed tokenizer nuance — multilingual CJK sequences produce different subword splits vs UTF-8 whitespace languages. when prefix caching is enabled, the cache key used byte offsets -> if tokenization splits differ between client and server or between runs, the kv cache alignment can shift by one token.
jin_zhang: good call. two separate problems: 1) kernel selection using wrong dims -> fallback slowdown, 2) tokenizer-induced cache misalignment making fallback-triggered kernels operate on shifted KV offsets which can corrupt attention.
perf-bot: snapshot: baseline p50=43ms p99=190ms; canary (post-change) p50=51ms p99=430ms; throughput -18%.
devops-bot: rolled canary back to previous image at 03:45 UTC while triage continues.
noah: quick mitigation proposal: prefer model.json n_heads & kv_head_dim if present, otherwise run a lightweight sanity check on inferred dims and assert (shape % head_dim == 0) and compare with expected param counts before choosing optimized kernel. fallback should be safe but avoid thrashing.
samir: patch in progress: add config-first kernel selector + warning log and metric (kernel_mismatch_detected). PR: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/8421 (draft).
alex_g: tokenizer mitigation: change kv-cache key from (token_index) to (token_index, byte_offset, tokenizer_version). that will make mismatched splits less likely to collide. also add a debug-mode assertion for cache hits verifying sequence prefix equality.
katie_s: note about ALiBi vs RoPE: ALiBi variants apply per-head slopes; if head ordering is misinterpreted, the slope mapping is wrong and attention weights diverge. selector must map alibi_type->per_head expectations and verify num_heads match.
jin_zhang: added unit tests for: a) qwen2.5 exported layout permutations, b) alibi/head mapping, c) multilingual tokenizer roundtrips for prefix cache.
noah: after rollback numbers look good — perf back to baseline on canary images we reverted to. once PR merges we should canary again with additional canary-only metrics for kernel_mismatch_detected and kv_cache_miss_reason.
alex_g: action items: samir -> finish selector PR and add metric (ETA 6h), jin_zhang -> add tokenizer roundtrip test and kv-cache key change (ETA EOD), katie_s -> validate ALiBi/head mapping on mixtral/mistral configs (ETA tomorrow), noah -> run extended canary and watch perf windows.
katie_s: :thumbsup: and filing an incident note for the rollback.
perf-bot: follow-up alert scheduled if p99 > 2x baseline during next canary.
alex_g: thanks team — big lesson: prefer explicit model metadata over shape heuristics, and make cache keys robust to tokenizer variability. will post a short postmortem after PRs land.
